items.title: Parallel Commutator
items.note: Valentina Magaletti, João Pais Filipe and Leon Marks make two long pieces of clattering polyrhythm under synth haze. The Quietus made it Album of the Week.
items.source: The Quietus, The Line of Best Fit

items.title: Corps Perdu
items.note: Fofana turns the words of Aimé Césaire and others into sound. It is heavy and quiet at once.
items.source: a closer listen, Fall Music Preview

items.title: Somewhere Between
items.note: The follow-up to On The Inside, with guests including Rosie Lowe and Matt Maltese. Warm, loose and soulful.

items.title: Chinese Benefits
items.note: Louis Johnstone, of Wanda Group, mixes stream of consciousness spoken word, abrasive noise and fractured electronics. Short tracks, odd and prickly.

items.title: Eyes Bright and Low
items.note: Ambient leaning, with a ten minute title track and a guest vocal from Rachael Lavelle. Described as light waves crashing on an autumn shore.
items.source: a closer listen, Fall Music Preview

items.title: Hits Different
items.note: The second album from the Kraków jazz group, after Jazz Report From The Hood. It shifts to a narrator's point of view.

items.title: Lost Meridians
items.note: Music to pause to, inspired by open prairies. One long title piece, and some short ones.
items.source: a closer listen, Fall Music Preview

items.title: Answers
items.note: Fully instrumental, recorded remotely between Wales and Austria. Tape warmed guitar on one side, liquid synth on the other. Lead single is "Lichen Trip".

items.title: Through to Us
items.note: Experimental compositions built on nature recordings, birdsong, synths and a piano passage. The title track runs about eight minutes.

items.title: Live at Keystone Korner
items.note: A posthumous live set from the organist, recorded in 2022. Eight tracks, with long takes on "Lady G" and "Vibrations in Blue".

items.title: Edge Conditions
items.note: Out October 9 on International Anthem. Eleven tracks of electronic music that AllMusic hears as 90s post-rock meeting experimental electro, with Booker Stardrum and Takako Minekawa along. Worth it for the band feel inside the machines.

items.title: Opening
items.note: Reversed acoustic instruments and stretched vocal samples, and it leans on unease through simplicity. Quiet, strange and patient.

items.title: Nightlife
items.note: Western Vinyl. Modular synth with Greg Fox on drums and Matt Bauder on sax and flute, made in late night sessions. Spacious and a bit like a small band playing in a dark room.

items.artist: Lothar Ohlmeier / Isambard Khroustaliov / Rudi Fischerlehner
items.title: Landscapes
items.note: Third album from this Berlin trio on Not Applicable. Bass clarinet, drums and electronics, free improv that nods to musique concrete and punk.

items.title: Testing the Waters
items.note: A long electroacoustic piece in five movements, first made for WDR 3 radio in Cologne in 2023. Field recordings and slow detail.

items.title: Ama Lel Hawa
items.note: Mostly solo oud, rooted in maqam, with three ensemble pieces that open it up gently. Her first solo full length. Warm and close.

items.title: Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three)
items.note: Out October 2 on Ndeya. Music from his Pentimento Trilogy. Worth a listen for that fourth-world trumpet haze.

items.title: Radical Frame
items.note: Musique concrete mixed with club-ready production. A strange, dense record.

items.title: Phren
items.note: A collaboration between a producer and a guitarist. Listed as ambient and experimental.

items.title: Waters Dance
items.note: Listed as jazz on Bandcamp. I found little else, so this one is a hunch.

items.title: Cyano
items.note: Out on RVNG Intl. Ambient, experimental electronic, from a reliably calm writer.

items.title: LUMINA
items.note: The Italian duo moves electronics to the centre, with synths and club rhythms beside oud, cello and vibraphone.

items.title: AT/DC
items.note: Warm guitar and banjo with reverb and synth. Described as close to Rain Drinkers.

items.title: RUIN: It's Not Just Music
items.note: Ambient, experimental electronic. I could not find more detail than that.

items.title: Friction
items.note: Out on Dragon's Eye Recordings. Field recordings with wordless vocals and a sense of endless space.

items.title: Baby Ghost
items.note: Falsetto voice mixed with bowed double bass, which gives it an otherworldly feel.

items.title: Linda's Head
items.note: Guitar songs that drift and smudge, on Grouper's own label. Quiet, strange and worth the full run.

items.title: Last Light of the Sun
items.note: Ambient, IDM, dub techno and a little drum and bass, with bamboo flute and typewriter in the mix. Soft on top, with real movement underneath.

items.title: Neram Pularumbol
items.note: Kerala drumming, drones and club bass, followed by a second half of remixes. Heavy in places, but it treats tradition as something alive.

items.title: Passing the Cup of Sorrows 1.1
items.note: The first piece from his album due 23 October. Tape-loop ambient, slow and sad.

items.title: Archives
items.note: Homemade instruments and chopped samples, built remotely between rural France and a London boat. The Quietus hears Autechre reworking The Wicker Man. Raw and odd.

items.title: SÖWT
items.note: Tenor saxophone drawing on Moroccan Gnawa tradition, set against blues-rooted jazz. A good one for a long evening.

items.title: Songs for Sad Poets Vol. III
items.note: Drone that breaks into short bursts out of long silence. Dark, patient and well suited to headphones.

items.title: Post Dub Cities
items.note: Austere dub-leaning electronics that sound like empty streets and wear. Cold and spare, in a good way.

items.title: Psychic Video
items.note: A preview from his DJ-Kicks mix, out 16 October. Dark, textured club music.

items.title: Shell and Core
items.note: Arabic-language post-rock and jazz, about lives left unfinished, like abandoned buildings.

items.title: Traces of Light
items.note: A saxophone quartet in quiet, searching post-bop, nine originals. The gentle pick of the week.

items.title: Alive Alone, Alive Together
items.note: Live guitar from four cities, fuzz and blues running through it, with Hamid Drake on drums for four tracks.

items.title: No Bad Memories
items.note: Their first album in six years, and it sounds like it. A sun soaked collage of samples and guest vocals, very much in the spirit of Since I Left You.

items.artist: Enrico Rava Fearless Five with Joe Lovano
items.title: Corners
items.note: Rava's quintet with Joe Lovano sitting in, recorded in Rome. Loose and lyrical, with the kind of chemistry you only get from players who've logged this many years together.

items.title: Chinese Benefits
items.note: Louis Johnstone, who also records as Wanda Group, mixing stream of consciousness spoken word with harsh noise and broken electronics. Bleak and bracing.

items.title: Follow The Light
items.note: Her debut, blending dub reggae with vintage psych folk and classic soul, shaped by growing up in a Jamaican household in South Florida. Warm and unhurried.

items.title: Hippies, Thugs and Heroes
items.note: His 20th studio album, and one of his strongest in years. The songwriting leads, the band stays tight behind him, and the guitar work is there without ever showing off.

items.title: Dopamine Chamber
items.note: Fifth album, picked up a five star review this week. Denser and more unsettled than what came before, but still unmistakably them.

items.title: In Time And Spirit
items.note: A London sextet led by guitarist Jean de Talhouët, built around a three part title suite with contrapuntal writing. Unusually optimistic for contemporary jazz.

items.title: Live at the Globe
items.note: Canadian guitar legend Lorne Lofsky and Nigel Price trading lines live in the north of England, recorded last November. Conversational, unhurried guitar jazz.

items.title: Back to The Halcyon
items.note: A joint EP marking five years of IMOGEN's WIGS label. White knuckle rave nostalgia, unapologetically maximalist.

items.title: Chronicles of Gnowt (Vol 2)
items.note: Second in Gnod's new triptych, heavy and repetitive with dub abstraction and spoken word running through the centerpiece track. Technically out October 9th, but too good to leave out.

items.title: Music Is Invisible (Pentimento Volume Three)
items.note: Previously unheard trio recordings of the late Fourth World pioneer, reworking themes from across his catalogue. It completes a trilogy he never lived to finish and it's the closest thing to a lost Hassell album we're going to get.

items.title: Melting Pillars of Snow
items.note: Contrabass recorder, shō, bowed cymbals and tape loops of spoken W.G. Sebald, with Swans' Michael Gira turning up on one track. Dense, slow-building electroacoustic work. Needs a dark room and your full attention.

items.title: Allison de Groot & Rich Ruth
items.note: A bluegrass banjo player and an ambient synth producer from Nashville, out on Western Vinyl. Clawhammer banjo through looping and delay set against pedal steel, strings and field recordings of cicadas. The two sounds never fully merge, which is what makes it work.

items.title: Lumina
items.note: Italian duo mixing drum machines and arpeggiators with oud, cello, xylophone and vibraphone. More club-facing than their earlier records but still unmistakably their own thing, world music that doesn't sound like a pastiche.

items.title: Nearly
items.note: Nathan Jenkins' first solo album in two years, made across London, Toronto and Montreal. Vocal-led electronic pop with L Devine guesting, understated and well-arranged rather than flashy. A grower.

items.title: Ruin: It's Not Just Music
items.note: A hard swerve from her usual modular ambient work into jungle, drum & bass and future garage, most of it past 170 BPM. Still unmistakably her, just with teeth.

items.title: Eugene / Save The World
items.note: Two sides of UK soul from Nao, one tender, one more upbeat. Not a huge event release but a genuinely good pair of songs.

items.title: Last Light of the Sun
items.note: Amsterdam producer hopping between ambient, techno, dub, dream pop and drum & bass across one record without it feeling scattered.

items.title: Archives
items.note: New studio album despite the title, the trio swapping instruments and working remotely across different cities. A collage of postmodern songcraft, warm and a bit woozy rather than clinical.

items.title: All For Free
items.note: A Juno Daily exclusive this week. Dub-inflected downbeat, slow and spacious.
